chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Alton Redd's origins and playing; Red Mack
summary: Howard says Alton Redd played the blues in many bands but never with him; Red Mack was a good trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Let's get to Alton Red. Remember Alton Red?
Yes, sure, I do. I Remember him? Sure, I do. He played with me for the longest time.
Where did you meet him and where was he from, you know? What city?
Where did Alton come from?
I don't know.
Do you remember when you met him?
Louisiana.
Louisiana?
He was from Louisiana.
When did he come to Los Angeles, do you have any idea?
No, I don't. I'm not going to --
I think (inaudible) family came when he was quite small, going to school. I'm sure of that.
Did you guys work together very much,
Oh, yeah.
In your band, or what bands, do you remember?
It wasn't in my band, it was just in different bands. He could play the blues pretty good with other bands. That's all he did. Never played with me.
Red Mack.
Red Mack? Oh, boy. He was a good one. He was a good trumpet player. I don't know where he got that playing from, but he could play. Could play yet, and a song yesterday.
You did?
Yeah.
Have no idea where his home town is or whatever?
No, I don't know. But what I do --
